memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "If anyone gives a neighbor silver or goods for safekeeping and they are stolen from the neighbor's house, the thief, if caught, must pay back double. But if the thief is not found, the owner of the house must appear before the judges, and they must determine whether the owner of the house has laid hands on the other person's property." - Exodus 22:7-8 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Life together depends on trust. Someone hands you their valuables for safekeeping — a beautiful act of confidence in your character. God's law takes that trust seriously. If the goods go missing, the matter must be examined honestly before judges to determine whether the keeper was faithful or had helped himself to what was not his. God will not let entrusted things be quietly pocketed.

This reveals how much God values faithfulness in the small, unseen dealings of everyday life. It is easy to be honest when everyone is watching. The test comes when something valuable is placed in your hands and no one would know if you kept a little for yourself. God knows. He sees the private choices that reveal who we really are.

Ultimately, everything we hold is entrusted to us by God — our money, our time, our gifts, our very lives. We are stewards, not owners. One day we will give an account for how faithfully we handled what He placed in our care (Luke 16:10-12). The good news is that God is not looking for perfection but for faithfulness. Be trustworthy with what is entrusted to you today, in the small things as much as the large.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Am I faithful with what others — and God — have entrusted to me?
Where am I tempted to be dishonest when no one is watching?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, everything I hold belongs to You. Make me faithful and trustworthy with what is entrusted to me, honest in the unseen places where only You can see. Amen.
